$comment: Maintainer ruling 2026-09-12: Copilot supplies the sole automated review round. A separate APPROVED review is not required; the maintainer's human merge decision remains outside this automated readiness verdict. AUDITED 2026-09-18 -- this file is VALID at nen 0.10.0 and the empty default_approvers is DELIBERATE, said here rather than by omission, which is exactly what the loader demands. `approval_policy: "review-round-only"` is NOT inert: it is the key that makes the empty approval set legal, and it is load-bearing in both directions. Measured against the installed 0.10.0 binary: `nen schema check --repo .` reports `ok nen/gates.json`, and `nen pr ready <n> --gh-repo zheref/hatsu` evaluates normally (#76 -> not-ready, a reviewer round still owed at head). DELETE `approval_policy` and the same loader refuses: `at default_approvers, is empty. An empty approval set makes the approve limb of the readiness gate VACUOUSLY TRUE ...`. Set it to anything else and it refuses too: `at approval_policy, expected 'required' or 'review-round-only'`. A grep finding no consumer for `review-round-only` in a zheref/nen source tree means that CHECKOUT predates the feature -- it landed in nen 0.10.0 (nen #209, PR #210; release PR #211), which is why nen/contract.json raises `minimum` to 0.10. Check the checkout version before reading an absence as evidence. So: do not "fix" this file by populating default_approvers, and do not remove approval_policy as dead configuration. Doing either changes the readiness verdict for every Hatsu pull request.

delivery.$comment: Current local delivery branches use the Codex prefix and the maintainer credentials.

$check_exclusions: Hatsu's own key (zheref/hatsu#104): a maintainer's ruling that a named check is not watched has this declared home and no other -- never a chat line, never a subagent brief. One row per ruling: {"name": "<the check name exactly as the rollup reports it>", "reason": "<why>", "ruled": "<YYYY-MM-DD>", "until": "<YYYY-MM-DD, or 'condition: <what lifts it>'>"}. Because every live row's name becomes one argv element of `nen pr ready --exclude-check`, a name is letters, digits, spaces and . _ / ( ) - only -- no comma (the flag's separator, zheref/nen#243), no quote, no shell metacharacter, no control byte -- and a row that cannot be passed safely is refused at the declaration (scripts/tenkai_adopt.sh diagnose, DRIFT) and NEVER put on the call: the verdict is read without it. A near-miss date in `until` is refused, never read as a condition; a condition row is re-examined every 90 days from `ruled`; a row past its date is DRIFT. The skills that read readiness (pr-state § 2 owns the rule; sharingan, en, getsuga through en) pass every live row by name and quote the verdict with the exclusion named; an EMPTY rollup after exclusion is not-ready by nen's own rule. nen preserves the key as raw data; validating it is zheref/nen#249. An empty array is a decision: nothing is excluded here.

exhausted.reason: Copilot review credits exhausted for the account

reviewer_fallback.$comment: Hatsu's own key -- the maintainer's ruling of 2026-09-29 (docs/ROSTER.md § Rulings of 2026-09-29; sharingan § 6 states the rule once, PROCESS § Reviewer rounds the mechanics): when a configured reviewer's credits are exhausted, the next reviewer in `chain` is requested where the gate knows its identity (Cursor's review bot is declared in reviewers[] once the app is installed; until then a chain step with no identity is missing-configuration), and when the chain is exhausted the local hanten rounds ARE the review and the PR is presented at its merge prompt with nen pr ready's verdict quoted as it stands -- not-ready (CON-32(b): reviewer <name> exhausted), never 'ready'. Rows are shaped as check_exclusions rows are (a name, a reason, a ruled date, an until date or condition); nen reads neither key -- an exhausted-reviewer read in pr ready is the owned dependency zheref/nen#275.

round_policy.$comment: Maintainer's rulings of 2026-09-19 (zheref/hatsu#85) and the ceiling of zheref/hatsu#102 (#69's specification). stallMinutes is read by nen pr ready (v0.11.0): a pending review request older than it reads not-ready: reviewer round stalled. minRounds (N) and maxRounds (M) are Hatsu's own keys, read by the skills (sharingan § 6 owns the rule): an owed reviewer round is requested on the maintainer's behalf, only through nen pr request-reviews, only while this PR's requested rounds are under maxRounds AND its resolved rounds are under minRounds; once minRounds resolved rounds exist no further round is requested -- 'owed at head' after the run's own push or request is not a reason; maxRounds with fewer than minRounds resolved is the reported blocker, nen pr ready --explain quoted, never a number raised in-session. monitor.maxCycles in nen/workflow.json is a different number -- en's ACTING-cycle cap.
